{{Short description|Exact solution to Einstein's field equations}}
{{technical|date=October 2013}}
{{general relativity|solutions}}

In [[general relativity]], the '''Weyl–Lewis–Papapetrou coordinates''' are used in solutions to the [[vacuum]] region surrounding an [[axisymmetric]] distribution of [[mass–energy]]. They are named for [[Hermann Weyl]], Thomas Lewis, and [[Achilles Papapetrou]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Weyl |first=Hermann |year=1917 |title=Zur Gravitationstheorie |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/andp.19173591804 |journal=[[Annalen der Physik]] |language=de |volume=359 |issue=18 |pages=117–145 |bibcode=1917AnP...359..117W |doi=10.1002/andp.19173591804 |issn=0003-3804}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lewis |first=T. |year=1932 |title=Some special solutions of the equations of axially symmetric gravitational fields |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Containing Papers of a Mathematical and Physical Character |language=en |volume=136 |issue=829 |pages=176–192 |bibcode=1932RSPSA.136..176L |doi=10.1098/rspa.1932.0073 |issn=0950-1207 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first=A. |last=Papapetrou |title=A static solution of the equations of the gravitatinal field for an arbitrary charge-distribution |journal= [[Proceedings of the Royal Irish Academy]]. Section A: Mathematical and Physical Sciences|volume=52 |pages=191–204 |year=1948 |jstor=20488481 }}</ref>

==Details==
The square of the [[line element]] is of the form:<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Bičák |first1=Jiří |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Hen4Bb-bjgUC |title=Gravitation, following the Prague inspiration: a volume in celebration of the 60th birthday of Jiří Bičák |last2=Semerák |first2=O. |last3=Podolský |first3=Jiří |last4=Žofka |first4=Martin |date=2002 |publisher=[[World Scientific]] |isbn=978-981-238-093-7 |editor-last=Bičák |editor-first=Jiří |location=River Edge, N.J |page=122 |oclc=ocm51260088 |editor-last2=Semerák |editor-first2=O. |editor-last3=Podolský |editor-first3=J. |editor-last4=Žofka |editor-first4=M.}}</ref>

:<math>ds^2 = -e^{2\nu}dt^2 + \rho^2 B^2 e^{-2\nu}(d\phi - \omega dt)^2 + e^{2(\lambda - \nu)}(d\rho^2 + dz^2)</math>

where <math>(t, \rho, \phi, z) </math> are the cylindrical Weyl–Lewis–Papapetrou coordinates in <math>3+1 </math>-dimensional [[spacetime]], and <math>\lambda </math>, <math>\nu </math>, <math>\omega </math>, and <math>B </math>, are unknown functions of the spatial non-angular coordinates <math>\rho </math> and <math>z </math> only. Different authors define the functions of the coordinates differently.
